data.description:
## Goal

Prevent ruff (the Python linter) from mis-parsing YAML and other non-Python configuration files as Python source, which produces false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings that pollute the Quality Improvement epic as auto-created work items. The fix MUST be **additive**: it must not hardcode any project-specific path (e.g. `proxy/config-cheap.yaml`), must not break scanning of other projects, and must never hide genuine Python findings in `.py` files in any project.

## Background / Root cause

The llm project Quality Improvement epic **LP-0MT1F4IQU00828FC** accumulated **155 false-positive child work items** (2026-08-20), all ruff `invalid-syntax` errors reported against `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — a YAML file being linted as Python (Unexpected indentation, Invalid annotated assignment target, Expected an expression, etc.).

The existing explicit-file-argument filter (commit e910f02d, `_run_ruff_check` / `_run_ruff_fix_mode`) only excludes TS/JS extensions and only in the `files=` branch. Two gaps remain:
1. The **whole-project scan path** (`files=None`, the `else` branch) runs `ruff check <root>` with only a TS/JS `--extend-exclude` — it does NOT exclude `.yaml`/`.yml` or other non-Python config files.
2. The current exclusion list is English-agnostic about additivity — it must be extended to cover non-Python config extensions generically so the fix holds for ANY project (not just llm), while never suppressing genuine findings.

Related existing item: **SA-0MSTMAPL40019JX5** addresses the explicit-file-argument path in the audit runner. This item covers the whole-project scan path and generalises the exclusion so it is additive across all projects.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The whole-project ruff scan path (`files=None`) excludes non-Python configuration extensions (at minimum `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.json`, `.toml`, `.md`) so ruff never mis-parses them, via `--extend-exclude`/`--force-exclude` — not by hardcoding any project-specific filename.
2. Genuine ruff findings on `.py` files are unaffected: existing tests pass and no Python lint is suppressed.
3. The fix is additive — works for any project root (verified with a non-llm project containing a `.yaml` file), with no hardcoded absolute paths or project names in the exclusion logic.
4. A regression test asserts that scanning a project tree containing a `.yaml` file (both a whole-project scan and an explicit-file scan) produces zero findings for that YAML file, while a `.py` file with a genuine issue still yields its finding.
5. The change is documented in the linter_runner module docstring/comment (both the explicit-file and whole-project paths).
data.title: Ruff: exclude YAML & non-Python files additively across all projects (whole-project scan)

Mirrors ContextHub epic child WL-0MVAPF1QM005FYM1 (epic WL-0MVAMS4RO000H3B0). The needsProducerReview flag and  were restored on ContextHub dev (F2/F3); the producer-hold assignee convention is RETIRED (Q2=C). This item reverses SA-0MV9DUE6F006SK1H, which re-homed the ship gate onto the assignee sentinel.

## Goal

As the release pipeline, I want check-final-validation.js to block release on items with needsProducerReview === true again (the restored flag), so shipment safety keys on the producer-review signal the operator restored.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js blocks release while any in-scope item has needsProducerReview === true without a passing audit ('Ready to close: Yes').
- [ ] check-audit-gate.js and run-release.js updated consistently (flag-based review check; no assignee-sentinel reference).
- [ ] No release-safety weakening: scenarios that previously blocked on the flag still block; assignee is no longer used as the producer-review signal (scheduling holds only).
- [ ] Tests cover: flagged unreviewed item blocks release; flagged reviewed item allows release; unflagged item behaves as today.
- [ ] Documented interface (from ContextHub F1): the flag is restored and read via wl show --json needsProducerReview; wl reviewed <id> toggles it.

## Key Files

- skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js, check-audit-gate.js, run-release.js
- skill/ship/tests/

## Related work

- ContextHub WL-0MVAPF1QM005FYM1 (delivery mirror), WL-0MVAMS4RO000H3B0 (epic)
- SA-0MV9DUE6F006SK1H (the re-homing being reversed)

data.description:
Mirrors ContextHub epic child WL-0MVAPF1QM005FYM1 (epic WL-0MVAMS4RO000H3B0). The needsProducerReview flag is restored and the producer-hold assignee convention is RETIRED (Q2=C). This item reverses the producer-marking part of SA-0MV98PAT7005VXXS while KEEPING its assignee-clear-on-terminal-verdicts behaviour.

## Goal

As the delivery pipeline, I want the audit runner to mark an item needsProducerReview=true on a 'yes' verdict (via wl update --needs-producer-review yes) so the release gate (restored by the sibling SA item) sees the producer-review state, instead of assigning the producer sentinel.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] audit_runner.py 'yes' verdict path sets needsProducerReview=true (wl update --needs-producer-review yes) instead of assigning the producer sentinel.
- [ ] KEEP: audit_runner clears the assignee on every terminal verdict (success 'yes', failure restore, verdict 'no') so the status-neutral claim is released.
- [ ] Failure-restore and abort-recovery (SIGKILL state-file) restore completed/in_review (no in-progress/in_review hybrid; WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL fix preserved).
- [ ] Tests cover: yes-verdict sets the flag; no-verdict/failure clear both flag and assignee; lifecycle unit + integration green.

## Key Files

- skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py
- skill/audit/tests/

## Related work

- ContextHub WL-0MVAPF1QM005FYM1 (delivery mirror)
- SA-0MV98PAT7005VXXS (producer-marking being reversed; assignee-clear kept)
- SA-0MV9DUE6F006SK1H (ship gate sibling)
data.title: Audit runner: set needsProducerReview on 'yes' verdicts (revert assignee-hold producer marking, keep assignee clear-on-terminal)
